recent_posts.title: Three React Three Fiber architecture mistakes and how to fix them
recent_posts.summary: Three common architectural mistakes when building React Three Fiber applications: mixing React renders with the Three.js frame loop (solved by using a mesh registry for real-time updates), making everything reactive in state management (fixed by using non-reactive mutations for visual side effects), and placing logic in React components instead of frame-based systems (resolved by creating dedicated systems with useFrame). These patterns improved performance and code maintainability in a 3D editor rewrite.

recent_posts.title: Horizontal development prioritizes shipping over perfection
recent_posts.summary: Horizontal development prioritizes building complete features quickly over perfecting individual components early. This approach involves drafting the entire system first with basic functionality, then refining layer by layer. While this creates messy code and architectural problems initially, it enables faster learning from real use cases and prevents wasted effort on premature optimization. The strategy accepts technical debt as a necessary trade-off for discovering actual requirements before committing to complex architecture.

Building 3D AI chatbots with React Three Fiber and n8n
recent_posts.summary: Learn to build immersive 3D AI chatbots using React Three Fiber without backend code. The tutorial covers integrating multiple LLMs (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude) through n8n workflows, implementing real-time lip sync with custom audio processing, creating 3D character animations with blend shapes, and adding visual effects like snow particles and bloom. The stack uses n8n for no-code AI automation, ElevenLabs for text-to-speech, and custom libraries for lip synchronization, resulting in production-ready chatbot experiences with voice interaction and animated 3D characters.

recent_posts.title: Building a 3D item placement system for walls and ceilings with Three.js
recent_posts.summary: Building a 3D item placement system requires handling grid, wall, and ceiling interactions through a scene graph architecture. The implementation uses nested nodes to represent buildings, levels, walls, and items, with separate tools for each placement type. Events are emitted from renderers (grid, wall, ceiling) and consumed by item tools to handle placement logic. Items are categorized by attachment type (floor, wall, wall-side, ceiling) in a catalog, enabling automatic rotation calculation based on surface normals and collision detection across different surfaces.

recent_posts.title: Why 3D Walls Look Terrible at Corners - And How to Fix It (Three.js)
recent_posts.summary: Explores the technical challenge of rendering clean wall junctions in 3D home editors, where simple box geometries create overlapping artifacts at corners. The solution involves calculating junction points based on wall thickness and angles, then splitting wall edges to create proper mitering. The approach prototypes the geometry problem in 2D using SVGs before implementing it in Three.js by creating custom shapes with additional vertices and extruding them along the Z-axis.

recent_posts.title: Three.js CSG Wall Cutouts - DevLog #1
recent_posts.summary: A technical walkthrough of implementing CSG (Constructive Solid Geometry) operations in Three.js to create wall cutouts for doors and windows in a browser-based 3D home editor. The tutorial demonstrates using the three-bvh-csg library with React Three Fiber to subtract geometries from walls, starting with simple shapes and progressing to complex window models imported from Blender. Key techniques include optimizing 3D models by creating simplified collision geometries, applying proper transformations, and debugging with visual operation modes.

recent_posts.title: Create an Infinite 3D Gallery with Three.js & VIVERSE
recent_posts.summary: Step-by-step guide to building an infinite 3D photo gallery using Three.js and React Three Fiber, integrated with the VIVERSE platform. Demonstrates creating a collaborative web experience where users can pose avatars with accessories and backgrounds, take screenshots, and share them in an ever-expanding gallery world.

recent_posts.title: How to Bake AO, PBR, and High to Low Poly with Blender for Three.js
recent_posts.summary: Learn advanced 3D texture baking techniques including PBR (Physically Based Rendering), ambient occlusion, and high-to-low poly workflows using Blender for Three.js web projects. The tutorial covers converting complex Blender materials into web-compatible textures, optimizing high-poly models for web performance while maintaining visual quality, and implementing different baking strategies for static versus dynamic lighting scenarios.

recent_posts.title: How to Bake Lighting with Blender for Three.js
recent_posts.summary: Light baking is a technique to pre-render lighting information from Blender into textures for Three.js scenes. The process involves creating proper UV maps, using tools like Simple Bake plugin to automate the workflow, and packing UV islands efficiently to maximize texture quality. Key steps include preparing objects with subdivision modifiers applied, creating dedicated UV maps for baking, using proper margin settings to avoid artifacts, and organizing objects into collections for batch processing. The result is realistic lighting and shadows in real-time 3D web applications without performance overhead.
